subject: C12
required_fixes: R1 [high] Make imported/catalog/stored Runtime cases consistent with the renderer contract. crates/desktop-core/src/library.rs:137 permits an object payload for any product, parse_import at :332 and parse_catalog reuse that validation, and CaseView projects a non-null payload. packages/desktop-contracts/src/client.ts:681 rejects every Runtime case with such a payload. Thus a bounded, otherwise valid import/catalog can be accepted and sealed, then invalidate shell snapshots, including after restart. The independent client-parser probe reproduced rejection of the producer-shaped projection; the v1 validator also permits this input. Acceptance: exercise import, catalog ingestion and restart through native parsing/projection and the real DesktopClient with a Runtime object payload. Either refuse it before modifying the library under an explicit compatibility rule or project it consistently and safely; no accepted case may break shell observation or enable unsupported execution.

R2 [medium] Keep inconsistent chart totals inside the wire contract. crates/desktop-core/src/observation.rs:406 computes per_mille whenever sessions > 0, even when violating > sessions. A chart with total=1 and violating=2 therefore produces per_mille=2000 while correctly reporting benign as unknown; client.ts:725 rejects ratios above 1000, invalidating the overview and its shell snapshot instead of showing the inconsistency gap. The independent real-parser probe reproduced that rejection and accepted the same overview with an unknown ratio. Acceptance: pass this literal chart through the production overview path and DesktopClient; show the source gap and unknown derived ratio without fabricated counts, contract errors or loss of other source data.

R3 [medium] Retain and retry failed library cleanup after tenant deletion. authority.rs:1911 removes the tenant durably and schedules ForgetLibrary; :2811 discards both the task result and library::forget's boolean. library.rs:569 can fail to remove the sealed file or derived Keychain key, and also ignores failure removing the unreadable backup. There is no durable library cleanup entry after the tenant disappears, so denial/locked storage/filesystem failure can leave orphaned data or keys indefinitely. Acceptance: inject key-deletion and file/backup-deletion failures, delete the tenant and restart, then restore storage access. Unfinished cleanup must remain observable and durable until every owned file/key is removed, without resurrecting the tenant or its library.

R4 [medium] Publish freshness and snooze deadline transitions while the app is idle. authority/observation_domain.rs:226 and :245 evaluate time only when a snapshot is constructed; authority.rs:1046 publishes snapshots on state changes. Neither the native start/subscription path nor OverviewInbox schedules deadline invalidation, and overview-inbox.tsx:66 trusts the last fresh flag. A fresh AllClear snapshot can remain displayed indefinitely and an elapsed snooze can remain hidden until unrelated native activity. The actual-component probe advanced the clock 601 seconds and triggered a local rerender: the face remained AllClear and status remained Updated. Acceptance: with no user action or remote response, crossing the ten-minute boundary publishes stale/gap state and crossing a snooze deadline restores the appropriate item; cover sleep/wake too. These local deadline updates can preserve D038's deferred remote polling policy.

R5 [medium] Distinguish admitted case saves/copies from their eventual outcome. authority/library_domain.rs:235 queues a SaveCase before the library opens; settle_library at :190 consumes pending cases and can later reject their merge as full/too large. runtime-view.tsx:80 immediately says Saved on admission and does not react to the later library problem/failure. CopyCase similarly announces Copied before an unopened destination accepts the pending case. A full or unavailable destination can therefore lose the queued addition while the originating view still reports success. The actual RuntimeView probe reproduced a persistent Saved message after a later full problem. Acceptance: hold library loading, request a Playground save or copy into an unopened full destination, then settle it; report the specific failure in the originating workflow and preserve recoverable input. Also expose protected-write failures and an explicit retry path, and show final saved/copied success only when established.
evidence_gaps: E1 [required native import/export evidence] C12's new NativeCasePicker in apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/adapters.rs is replaced by StagedCases under test-fixtures, and exports still use FixtureSaver instead of NativeSaver. acceptance_c12.py's C12-N04 proves staged-byte ingestion and fixture output, not the production NSOpenPanel/NSSavePanel flows. Supply source/build-bound native evidence with synthetic cases through the production picker/saver, covering choose/save, cancellation with no change, bounded-file refusal, confirmed overwrite/private output and keyboard/focus return. The older C10/C11 dialog gaps remain separate; their deferral does not establish this new C12 path.

E2 [required T01/T06/T23 evidence] The nine library_observation cases and current native driver do not establish C12's offline launch/local-change/restart workflow or delayed library import/catalog/copy/save isolation during tenant deletion, switching and reset. The native six-second reconnect check covers Overview requests, and the locked-library test covers opening, not failed protected writes or cleanup recovery. Add production-interface cases for offline Library use with no remote authority, preserved local changes across restart, explicit retry without scan/catalog/mutation replay, delayed completions bound to their original tenant, and locked/denied/interrupted write/deletion recovery. Bind the applicable offline workflow to native evidence. Include end-to-end producer/renderer cases for R1/R2 and clock-driven subscription cases for R4.
limitations: C12 is substantially implemented with focused Rust library/observation domains, shared presentation, explicit case loading without execution, protected storage and reproducible retained evidence. Native/renderer contract disagreement (R1/R2), incomplete cleanup lifecycle (R3), time-dependent projection (R4), asynchronous save reporting (R5) and missing mandatory evidence prevent a 9/10 pass. Scores were not raised to meet a threshold.
